name: Cyclopentasiloxane

lead: Cyclopentasiloxane, also called D5, is a lightweight silicone used as an emollient and carrier in skincare, sunscreens, deodorants, hair products and makeup. It helps the look of skin and hair by giving a smooth, silky slip and evaporating without a greasy feel, so primers, serums and foundations spread evenly.

A Cosmetic Ingredient Review expert panel concluded that cyclic siloxanes are safe in current practices of use, citing minimal skin absorption and no sign of irritation or sensitisation. Environmental regulation is separate: the EU limits D5 in rinse-off cosmetics.

paras: It appears in ingredient lists of primers, serums, foundations, sunscreens and hair-smoothing products, often near the top. It evaporates after application, leaving the other ingredients behind.

Safety review found minimal percutaneous absorption and no irritation or sensitisation signals. Concerns are mainly environmental, with D5 described as persistent and bioaccumulative in some assessments.

chain: Smooth, silky-looking skin and hair finish
angle.text: D5 makes creams, primers and hair products spread easily and feel smooth, improving how makeup and skincare look on skin.

lead: Cyclopentasiloxane, known as D5 or decamethylcyclopentasiloxane, is a colourless, odourless, slightly volatile silicone liquid used as an emollient in deodorants, antiperspirants, sunscreens, hair sprays, skin care and hair conditioners. [1]

Its appearance role is texture and finish. Because it spreads in a thin film and then evaporates, it gives primers, serums, foundations and hair-smoothing products a silky slip and a light after-feel, which helps makeup and skincare glide on evenly and look smooth. Hair-care research has also examined silicone conditioning agents on chemically straightened hair. [1]

A Cosmetic Ingredient Review expert panel assessed the cyclic siloxane group, reporting minimal skin absorption and concluding the ingredients are safe in present practices of use. [2] Separately, the EU treats D5 as a substance of very high concern on environmental grounds and has restricted it in cosmetics in stages, starting with rinse-off products on 31 January 2020. [1][3]
infobox: Rinse-off cosmetics under 0.1% since 2020; leave-on from 2027 [3]

paras: D5 is an organosilicon compound with the formula [(CH3)2SiO]5: a ring of five silicon-oxygen units, each carrying two methyl groups. It is a liquid that boils at about 210 C, is almost insoluble in water and is classed as a cyclomethicone, also called cyclopentamethicone. [1]

Industrially it is made from dimethyldichlorosilane, whose hydrolysis yields cyclic and linear dimethylsiloxanes; D5 is separated by distillation. It was first isolated in 1946 as a hydrolysis product of that precursor, and D4 and D5 also serve as building blocks for silicone polymers. [1]

Formulators use D5 as a volatile carrier and emollient. It lets a product spread easily and feel light rather than greasy, then evaporates and leaves the other ingredients (pigments, film formers, emollients, actives) on the skin or hair. [1]

It appears in the ingredient lists of makeup primers, foundations, serums, sunscreens and hair-smoothing or shine products, often alongside dimethicone, a non-volatile silicone that leaves a lasting smooth film.

In Canada, about 70% of consumer-product use was in antiperspirants and about 20% in hair care. D5 has also been used as a dry-cleaning solvent, marketed from the 1990s as an alternative to tetrachloroethylene. [1]

The Cosmetic Ingredient Review Expert Panel found minimal percutaneous absorption and no data suggesting skin irritation or sensitisation for the cyclic siloxanes, and concluded the ingredients are safe in present practices of use. [2]

Wikipedia reports that D5 is acutely non-toxic in rats (an LD50 above 50 g/kg), that it caused tumours in female rats in one study without further carcinogenicity evaluation, and that long-term effects on the liver and immune system have not been fully investigated. Its hazard classification includes a suspected reproductive-toxicity statement. [1]

Environmental regulation centres on persistence rather than skin safety. The EU identified D4, D5 and D6 as substances of very high concern for very persistent and very bioaccumulative properties. Commission Regulation (EU) 2018/35 of 10 January 2018 amended REACH Annex XVII, and since 31 January 2020 D5 cannot be placed on the EU market in wash-off cosmetics at 0.1% by weight or more. [1][3]

Trade press reports that the Commission has extended the 0.1% limit to leave-on cosmetics from 6 June 2027, and that ECHA expects the measure to reduce emissions of these siloxanes by up to 90%. [3] Use of D5 in dry cleaning is slated to be prohibited in the EU after June 2026. [1]

Other agencies reached different conclusions on environmental risk: a Canadian Board of Review report of 20 October 2011 concluded that D5 does not pose a danger to the environment, and an Australian Tier II assessment found direct risks to aquatic life at expected concentrations unlikely to be significant. [1]
No studies found. A toxicological safety assessment of the cyclic siloxane group exists. [2] A separate laboratory study compared conditioning agents on chemically straightened Afro-ethnic hair.
Cyclopentasiloxane belongs to the cyclomethicone family with D4 (cyclotetrasiloxane) and D6 (cyclohexasiloxane). D4 has been banned in EU cosmetics since 2018. [1][2][3]
